explanation: The theorem computes the relative index (in the adic-completion integer ring of L) of the intersection of two comaps: one along θ - mulLeft c (a K-linear operator built from an order-of-finite-order automorphism) and one along multiplication by ϖ^s, obtaining absNorm v.asIdeal ^ min s m. This is a highly specific local-field/herbrand-quotient computation. I grepped Mathlib for `adicCompletionIntegers` (only basic material in AdicValuation.lean, FinitePlace.lean, FiniteAdeleRing.lean, HeightOneSpectrum.lean, LaurentSeries.lean), for `AddSubgroup.relIndex` (index lemmas, covolume, det-based relIndex results in CardQuotient.lean, and Different.lean), and for the key notions `relIndex_pow_smul_top_comap`, `pow_smul_top_comap`, `finrank_ker_baseChange`, `absNorm_pow_min`, `relIndex_comap` — none of these computations exist in Mathlib. The proof here relies on the library's own results (`LinearMap.relIndex_pow_smul_top_comap_eq_card_pow_min_of_finrank_ker_baseChange_le_one`, `associated_det_fO`, etc.), which are not Mathlib declarations, and no single Mathlib statement (nor a one-two line instantiation of one) expresses this relative-index formula.
